title: Priming-phase prober and kernel confabulator for arch/length-aware runtime selection
creator: Marta Rodriguez
description: Design and implement a lightweight 'priming‑phase' probing mechanism plus an in‑memory kernel confabulator to select the best compute kernel at request onset. Target mixed workloads with variable architecture (A100, H100, T4) and variable init/continuation lengths. The goal is to reduce p95/p99 latency for bursty conversational traffic by selecting a kernel that balances throughput and tail latency without large probe overhead or cold-start regressions.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end rollout yields >=6% p95 latency reduction and >=10% p99 reduction on mixed conversational benchmark against baseline runtime-2.3 when using default traffic mix
Probe overhead does not increase mean token cost by more than 2% at steady state
No regression in total throughput (RPS) for Dedicated capacity tests under 95th percentile load
Confabulator falls back to safe kernel set with zero errors on edge-case opvariants
Feature gated and controlled via runtime flags; Console dashboard shows per-key selection telemetry
tech_notes: Priming-phase probe runs only during the initial prefill window (first 8 tokens or until attention cache populated) to avoid decode tail interference
Probe logic: microbench 3 light kernels (fast-attn, blocked-attn, nv1-tiling) with 2 short runs each, collect latency, occupancy, and SM utilization estimates
Fingerprinting: combine host arch tag, GPU memory headroom, sequence-length bucket (0-32,33-128,129-512,>512), and token-phase estimate (priming vs steady-state) into a 64-bit key for lookup
Confabulator: in-memory LRU store of (fingerprint -> ranked kernel list + confidence band). On low-confidence, use conservative hedging to prefer latency-stable kernels
Telemetry: new metrics required: probe_attempts, probe_latency_overhead, kernel_confidence_score, selection_source (cache|probe|heuristic), kernel_switch_count
Safety: probes must be cancelable if request latency SLO breaches; probe runs should cap at 20ms additional wall-time per request
Rollout strategy: staged canary (2% host traffic) -> 10% -> 50% with automatic rollback on 10% increase in p99 latency or error rate
Data retention: aggregate probe telemetry to 90 days for model retraining; raw microbench traces only 7 days to limit storage
decisions: Use priming-phase probing vs background continuous probing to minimize steady-state noise
Prefer in-memory confabulator (LRU) over a remote service to avoid added network variance
Bucket sequence-lengths coarsely to reduce cardinality and accelerate warmstarts
Apply hedging policy when confidence < 0.55; hedging selects kernel that historically minimized p99 within same fingerprint
tradeoffs: Exploration vs stability: more aggressive probing finds better optima faster but can destabilize tail latency
Memory vs accuracy: larger confabulator cache increases hit rate but consumes host memory; start with 1MB per host
Probe cost: short microbench runs add latency/cost; we limit probes to early tokens only and TTL cache to amortize expense
Complexity: additional telemetry and rollout controls add operational surface area that SRE must monitor
implementation_plan: Week 1: Spike — prototype priming probe harness in local runtime; validate microbench patterns and 20ms cap
Week 2: Build confabulator module (LRU store + persistence hooks), expose runtime flags and metrics
Week 3: Integrate probe into request pipeline; add cancellation hooks and hedging policy; unit + integration tests
Week 4: Internal canary on staging fleet; collect telemetry and adjust confidence thresholds
Week 5: Gradual production rollout with observability dashboard and alert rules; postmortem and tuning
